evals.prompt: I have a data-oriented ECS where a Transform component's position changes each frame. A physics engine keeps its own kinematic actor state that must reflect the ECS transform. How should I keep the physics side in sync with the ECS, and what should I watch out for? Sketch the approach.
assertions: Recommends a brute-force filter-and-batch system that re-pushes every matching entity's transform to physics each frame as the default, adding dirty/version flags or change lists only when profiling shows the external call dominates

Explicitly advises against propagating transform changes to physics via observer/on-changed callbacks because they fire outside the declared read/write dependencies and break the parallel scheduler (reserving callbacks for lifecycle only)
Notes the one-frame out-of-sync window from batch mirroring and says to order the mirror pass before any raycast/query that depends on it (or query the ECS-side value)

evals.prompt: In my ECS an entity can carry several lights (e.g. a lamp post with three bulbs). What's the right way to model an entity that has multiple lights, given the component storage is per-type contiguous arrays?
assertions: States that an entity should hold at most one instance of a given component type, so you should NOT attach the light component multiple times to the same entity
Represents the collection either as child entities each holding one light component, or as a single list-holding component (optionally with an index pointing into a system-private structure)
Justifies this by noting multiple instances would force (entity, type, instance-id) addressing / per-instance ids and lookup indirection instead of clean (entity, type) access

evals.prompt: Write the core loop for a movement system in a data-oriented archetype ECS that integrates position from velocity, and explain how it should be filtered and parallelized. Entities are stored grouped by component set with per-type contiguous arrays.
assertions: The loop walks the co-located transform and velocity arrays directly (raw pointer/index walk over the passed arrays plus a count) with no per-element entity-id/handle lookup and no cross-system call inside the loop
Filters by a required component mask, running over every bucket/archetype whose type is a superset of that mask
Parallelizes by splitting the entity count into ranges (one job per range) and declares/keeps the read and write component sets explicit so a scheduler can run non-conflicting systems concurrently

evals.prompt: I'm feeding a renderer from ECS data and there are multiple simultaneous viewers (main camera plus shadow and reflection views). How should I structure culling and per-object visibility so the render pass stays parallel-safe, and how do extra viewers like shadows get added?
assertions: Culls per viewer and records results as a per-renderable visibility bitmask (one bit per viewer), filling all bits in a single pass over the component data so each renderable is visited once for all viewers
States that extra viewers (shadows, reflections) are generated during render-graph execution and fold into the viewer array, and must NOT be registered before execution
